instagram.title: Israel's president tasks Eisenkot with forming government

slides.headline: Israel's president tasks Eisenkot with forming government
slides.subtitle: Neither major political bloc secured a majority last week

slides.explanation: Israel has a 120 seat parliament, meaning a party needs 61 seats to form a government. No single bloc reached that threshold in the recent election.

slides.headline: The election resulted in a deadlocked parliament
slides.explanation: Even with the election over, the country remains in limbo because neither Netanyahu nor his rivals can claim a governing majority.
Six independent news outlets including the BBC, NPR, and Al Jazeera have verified this political deadlock. This consensus confirms the current instability.

slides.subtitle: Read the full briefing on Headlinne

instagram.caption:
Israel faces a significant political challenge following last week's election results.

Neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor the opposition secured the necessary majority to form a stable government.

Because of this deadlock, the president has tasked opposition leader Eisenkot with the difficult job of building a coalition. This is a critical moment for the country's legislative future.

We are tracking how coalition talks develop as the political stalemate continues. Do you think a coalition will be formed quickly?
